messages.subject: Categorical data and standardized coefficients
parts:
I am little confused about categorical\binary data. according to the tutorial if it is an exogenous variable
than I don't need to declare it. (http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html).
Still I am not sure about the interpretation of standardized coefficients since they are
based on standard deviation and I don't know what does it mean for binary variable...
(of course It is possible to calculate, but still I think that interpretation is different)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Categorical data and standardized coefficients
parts:
You can calculate the M and SD of a binary variable.  The mean is the proportion in the 1 category, and the SD is the square-root of the variance, which I think should be similar to the variance calculated using the Bernoulli formula: p*(1 - p)

The interpretation is the same. When a binary variable increases 1 SD, the standardized slope is how many SDs the outcome changes.  But I agree that the interpretation is not very useful for categorical data.  Perhaps better to interpret the unstandardized effect of dummy codes.

Terry
